Community Showcase
Discover What Your Colleagues Have to Offer
Have you ever wondered what services, products, or expertise your fellow credential evaluation professionals bring to the field? The TAICEP community is filled with organizations doing innovative work, hosting specialized events, and developing valuable tools.
We invite all registered conference attendees, exhibitors, and sponsor organizations to showcase their work, highlight upcoming events, or share products and resources that benefit the international credential evaluation community. Whether you are launching a new tool, promoting a workshop, or simply building brand awareness for your institution, this space is for you!
What You Can Feature
Organizational Profiles:
Introduce your organization, mission, and services to build brand awareness within our global network.
Upcoming Events & Workshops:
Share details about your webinars, training sessions, or post-conference meetings.
Products & Services:
Highlight specialized software, evaluation tools, publications, or consulting solutions.
How to Submit Your Listing
This showcase is a free benefit available to all registered conference attendees and sponsors. To submit your listing, please email answers@taicep.org with the following details by
October 16, 2026
:
Organization & Contact Name
(Must be associated with a registered attendee or sponsor)
Short Description:
Maximum
150–200 words
Logo or Banner Image:
High-resolution PNG or JPG file
(Recommended size: 400x400 pixels or standard horizontal banner)
Website & Contact Links:
Direct URL for your product, event RSVP, or organization page
Note: Submissions are published on a rolling basis. Drafts may be edited slightly for length and formatting.

LANGUAGECERT Academic: Research-Backed Evidence for Informed Admissions Decisions
LANGUAGECERT Academic (LCA) is a four-skill English proficiency assessment designed for higher education, providing institutions with overall and individual skill scores on the LANGUAGECERT Global Scale (0–100), aligned to CEFR.
LCA is supported by an ongoing program of research and validation. A large-scale concordance study involving 1,008 test takers from 46 nationalities found a strong correlation (r=.87) between overall LCA and IELTS Academic performance, providing empirical evidence to support score interpretation and recognition decisions.
Institutions can securely access and verify candidate results through the LANGUAGECERT Scores Verification System.

Prospects HEDD
Prospects HEDD is the UK's trusted provider of degree verification and student data services.
Managed by Jisc, HEDD was launched in 2011 to help protect students, graduates, universities and employers from degree fraud. Since then, HEDD has become an established part of the verification process, providing secure online degree verification and a central degree fraud reporting service.
For employers, recruitment agencies and other organisations involved in hiring, HEDD provides a straightforward way to verify candidates' academic qualifications directly with higher education providers.
With more than two million verification enquiries processed since its launch, HEDD continues to support organisations to carry out robust pre-employment checks and protect against fraudulent qualifications.

Educational Credential Evaluators (ECE)
, a charter member of the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES), is a nonprofit public‑service organization founded in 1980. We evaluate international academic and professional qualifications to determine their U.S., Canadian, or global equivalents for purposes of further education, immigration, employment, and professional licensure. We envision a world where every person's achievements are recognized and understood globally, empowering individuals to pursue their dreams and expanding opportunity for all.
Through
ECE Aid™
, our philanthropic initiative, we provide free evaluation reports for refugees and other displaced populations, helping them rebuild their lives with dignity and access new opportunities.
For international admissions professionals and global credential evaluators,
ECE Connection™
serves as a comprehensive resource hub and collaborative forum. Its mission is to bring together practitioners worldwide to share information, access tools, and strengthen best practices in admission decision‑making, credential equivalency determination, professional standards, training opportunities, and global education research and insights.

Trusted credentials. Confident decisions. Global mobility.
TruMerit® supports the institutions and authorities responsible for making decisions about international healthcare credentials.
Supporting healthcare regulators worldwide
For nearly five decades, TruMerit has provided credential evaluation and verification services for nurses and other healthcare professionals. We work with regulatory and licensing authorities in the United States and around the world to authenticate credentials, assess international education, and support informed licensure decisions.
Helping U.S. institutions evaluate international education
Through
ICD, TruMerit's NACES-certified division
, we help U.S. colleges and universities evaluate the education of internationally trained applicants. Institutions benefit from our global knowledge of educational systems, proven evaluation processes, and individualized client support.
Advancing credential integrity
TruMerit produces research and practical insights on issues affecting credential evaluation and workforce mobility, including emerging fraud risks and international nurse migration.

Amala Education
is a not-for-profit reimagining what education can be for refugee and conflict affected youth. Our pioneering programmes are both life-changing opportunities for young people and a platform for developing, demonstrating and scaling approaches that others can adopt.
The
Amala Global Secondary Diploma programme
offers refugee and conflict affected youth aged 16-25 an internationally accredited (CIS, NEASC) pathway to complete their secondary education and engage with action and community impact. The programme takes a competency-based approach to assessment, where each demonstrated competency earns students credit toward the Amala Global Secondary Diploma, recorded in a digital transcript provided by the Mastery Transcript Consortium.
Our context-adaptive, project-based short courses foster entrepreneurship, bridge to further education and support sustainable livelihoods for a broader group of young people. Amala also trains local educators - over 400 to date - equipping them with the competencies to design, facilitate and improve transformative learning.
Through working in partnership with mission-aligned, often refugee-led organisations rooted in the communities where we work, we have reached over 10,000 young people in 14 countries living through conflict and displacement since 2017.
